title: POC: Workload cohorting & tail-latency traffic sketch — CascadeAI
summary: Discovery/PoC scoping to define traffic cohorts, tail-latency SLOs, token mixes and benchmark plan. Customer wants a 4-week pilot to validate cost/latency tradeoffs across hosted vs dedicated and to exercise KV/prefix caching. Key success: 99th latency under 450ms for high-priority cohort; reproducible replay benchmark with realistic token distributions; and a cost-per-1000-token target for production rollout.
next_steps: Redwood to provide preliminary sizing spreadsheet (QPS, concurrency, token mix) by 2026-06-03
CascadeAI to share 7-day anonymized request traces or sample logs by 2026-06-02
Schedule 60-min benchmark plan walk-through with engineering (Samir + Marta) week of 2026-06-07
Redwood to deliver initial synthetic replay harness and runs (1x small, 1x 10x burst) by 2026-06-10

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-30
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Koh (CascadeAI Head of Platform), Marta Ruiz (ML Eng), Owen Park (SRE)
Recording link: [redacted]

Summary/Context: Quick discovery then deep dive into traffic cohorts and benchmark design for a 4-week pilot. CascadeAI is migrating conversational routing + summarization endpoints and needs predictable tail latencies for premium customers.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got Dana, Marta, Owen from Cascade, and Samir and I from Redwood. Agenda is scoping the pilot: traffic cohorts, success criteria, and benchmark plan.
[00:20] Dana (CascadeAI): Yep, that's right. We have a couple constraints — must hit latency for paying customers, and we need to estimate cost per 1k tokens. We're also curious about caching, like K-V cache behavior, and how it affects tail.
[00:40] Samir (Redwood SE): Great. Can you describe current traffic shape? QPS peaks, typical concurrency, and token lengths? Even ballpark helps.
[01:05] Marta (CascadeAI): Sure. Average QPS across endpoints is about 25 qps, but premium cohort accounts for spikes to 220 qps for short bursts. Concurrency we see 40-120 depending on time of day. Input tokens are small — usually 12–35 tokens — output varies more, 40–180 tokens, with long-form summaries hitting 600+ tokens occasionally.
[01:40] Owen (SRE): To add: the bursts are highly correlated to batch jobs and user sessions — we call them 'episode' spikes. They last 30–90s usually.
[02:05] Lena: Good detail. For the pilot, do you have historical logs we can use for a replay, or do you prefer synthetic profiles?
[02:25] Dana: We can provide 7 days of anonymized request logs, yes. Need to strip PII — our security team will coordinate.
[02:40] Marta: One note — different endpoints have different success thresholds. Our routing service has three tiers: interactive-chat (SLO 200–300ms p50/p95), assistant-long (p50 500ms p95 1.8s), and batch-summarize where latency is less strict.
[03:10] Samir: That's helpful — we should define cohorts: high-priority (interactive-chat), mid (assistant-long), and background (batch). For sizing, we map percent of traffic and tail constraints.
[03:35] Lena: Quick qualification on infra — are you open to Redwood Dedicated or do you need to stay on Hosted for this pilot?
[03:50] Dana: For pilot we prefer hosted to reduce ops, but long-term dedicated is on the table if costs align. Key is we can evaluate both in the pilot if Redwood provides a dedicated-like config or comparable latency profile.
[04:15] Samir: We can run experiments: hosted baseline and a dedicated-simulated run (reserved pool) to compare. We'll also toggle quantization and KV prefix cache.
[04:35] Owen: On security, we'll want SOC2 specifics and KMS integration notes. If we ever go private we need VPC options, but not necessarily for pilot.
[04:55] Lena: We'll send the security checklist and the SOC2 report link. Also note HSM/KMS integration takes more time for private.
[05:10] Marta: Back to traffic modeling — how does Redwood want the token distribution? We can provide exact token histograms, but how do you consume that for benchmarking?
[05:30] Samir: We take histograms and then create a replay with matching token-length distribution, preserving input/output correlation when possible. Also we create cohorts with different request mixes and burst patterns.
[05:55] Dana: Important: prefix caching in our flows reduces average tokens for repeat requests. The KV cache matters for response tail — sometimes a cached prefix reduces latency dramatically.
[06:20] Samir: Right. We'll include cache-on and cache-off runs. For the pilot success metric, what's the threshold you care most about — p99, p95, 99.9?
[06:40] Dana: For interactive-chat it's p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 450ms. For assistant-long we accept p95 <= 1200ms.
[06:55] Lena: We'll codify that. Also cost goal? Any budget cap per 1k tokens or per user?
[07:10] Marta: Target cost is under $0.30 per 1k output tokens for production; pilot can be higher. But this is a rough internal target.
[07:25] Samir: OK. Practical benchmarking approach: 1) replay recorded traces at 1x, 5x, and 10x to stress tail, 2) steady-state runs to measure throughput and average latency, 3) synthetic worst-case long-seq runs (600+ tokens) to see memory pressure.
[07:55] Owen: For concurrency modeling, we need to map sessions-to-concurrency. Many requests are pipelined — user sends prompt then assistant next. So concurrency vs QPS mapping is nuanced.
[08:15] Lena: We'll want a short questionnaire from Cascade to understand session behavior and how you classify premium traffic.
[08:30] Dana: Happy to fill that. Also, we need to know which internal stakeholders will sign off on the pilot success — product, platform, finance?
[08:45] Marta: Sign-off will be Product (Ava), Platform (Dana), and Finance (Tom). They'll expect the final runbook and cost estimate.
[09:00] Samir: On metrics we'll produce: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail quantiles, token-per-request distributions, cost-per-1k tokens, and instance utilization. We'll also capture error rates and model output regressions if you provide eval prompts.
[09:30] Dana: Great. Regarding models: are you testing multiple model sizes? We want to see trade-offs between a small quantized model and a large higher-quality one.
[09:45] Samir: Yes — pilot can include two variants: model-A (quantized, lower latency) and model-B (higher quality, larger). We'll compare quality via a small eval set you provide.
[10:10] Lena: Logistics: Redwood supplies the harness and runs in our infra; we can also provide a remote runner that you run inside your VPC if you prefer. For pilot, hosted is easiest.
[10:30] Owen: If we run inside our VPC we'll need an on-prem connector and private control plane docs. Not for pilot though.
[10:45] Marta: How do you handle KV cache persistence between requests in replay? We want to simulate sessions with cache warmups.
[11:05] Samir: We'll replay sessions preserving user IDs so cache warms up. We'll also create entirely cold-start runs to measure penalty.
[11:30] Lena: Walkthrough of proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — agreements and logs shared. Week 1 — Redwood sizing and first synthetic runs. Week 2 — replay runs and mid-pilot tuning. Week 3 — peak stress tests and final cost/latency report. Does that align?
[11:55] Dana: That seems tight but doable. 4-week calendar is fine if we have some overlap on approvals.
[12:10] Samir: We need the logs by end of week to hit those dates. Also confirm which endpoints and percentage splits.
[12:25] Marta: We'll send endpoint mapping (interactive-chat 35%, assistant-long 45%, batch 20%). Bursts concentrated on interactive-chat.
[12:40] Lena: On measurement, we will instrument token-level tracing and produce per-route dashboards. We'll include latency heatmaps and QPS vs concurrency graphs.
[12:55] Owen: About tail-latency mitigation — can Redwood auto-fallback to smaller model on overload?
[13:10] Samir: We support fallback routing policies; we can route to cheaper/model-B under load, and also degrade gracefully by limiting response lengths or returning cached summaries. We'll show policy examples.
[13:30] Dana: Good. Cost modeling question: do you include batching and KV cache benefits in projected cost-per-1k?
[13:45] Samir: Yes, we'll produce two cost curves: naive per-token and optimized with batching/prefetching/cache. That usually shows 20–40% savings for bursty workloads.
[14:05] Marta: About benchmarks: we want reproducibility. Can you check in the harness to a repo and provide the exact command used?
[14:20] Samir: Yes, we'll give a reproducible repo and a runbook. Also, we'll export raw time-series for your team to ingest.
[14:35] Lena: Security deliverables — SOC2, data handling, KMS notes, and an NDA if needed. We'll attach those.
[14:50] Dana: We'll need to evaluate RTP (data residency) only for EU customers, but not in pilot.
[15:05] Owen: Regarding monitoring, can Redwood send tracing hooks? We want to integrate with our observability stack (Datadog).
[15:20] Samir: We have tracing hooks and can emit prometheus-compatible metrics and a small Datadog exporter.
[15:35] Marta: Success criteria recap: interactive-chat p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 450ms, cost < $0.30/1k tokens (target), reproducible replay and a signed runbook.
[15:55] Lena: We'll craft a formal success criteria doc and attach it to the pilot agreement.
[16:10] Dana: For the pilot contract do we need to lock usage caps? We don't want surprises on hosted billing during stress runs.
[16:25] Lena: We can set a temporary usage cap for the account and provide a bump request flow. We'll document that.
[16:40] Owen: Any red flags from Redwood about tokenization differences across models? E.g., whitespace vs BPE changes outputs and token counts.
[16:55] Samir: Good point — we'll standardize tokenization in the harness and report tokenization deltas. For quality we ask you to provide 20 eval prompts per endpoint.
[17:15] Marta: We'll prepare eval prompts and expected behaviors.
[17:30] Lena: Scheduling the technical bench walk-through: Samir will run it with Marta and Owen. Proposed slot: 60 minutes week of 2026-06-07.
[17:45] Dana: That works for us.
[18:00] Samir: Anything else?
[18:10] Dana: One small ask — can Redwood run an initial smoke test at low scale so we can validate instrumentation?
[18:25] Samir: Yes, we'll run a 30-minute smoke with token-level tracing and share dashboards.
[18:40] Lena: Ok last part — recap of next steps and owners. We'll send a follow-up email with attachments.
[18:55] All: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
notes: Call had natural transcription artifacts: 'KV' sometimes transcribed as 'K V', 'VPC' as 'V P C', and occasional speaker attribution errors. Meeting contained AE+SE presence and included qualification, benchmarking plan, and explicit next steps. Customer is open to hosted pilot but wants to compare dedicated-like run. Priorities: tail p99 gating for interactive customers and cost per token target.
